title: The reference says a domain is one business capability, and the domain-named-for-technology check calls it a vertical slice whose technology is its technical records
when: The reference is built.
then: The domain kind's description calls a domain one business capability, and the `domain-named-for-technology` check's explanation calls it a vertical slice whose technology is its technical records, linked from the kind's entry.

title: The modeling skill's first step finds the business capabilities and makes each a slice, with the questions that tell one from a layer
when: Reads the `model-a-domain` skill.
then: Expects its first section to find the business capabilities before any record is written, and to ask at least four questions that tell a capability from a layer.

title: Each domain says its subdomain type: core, supporting or generic
when: A domain is written with no subdomain type, and with one that is not core, supporting or generic.
then: The column is required and described; both rows are refused.

title: A capability sits under a domain with a required whole-number position, and every use case sits under one of its domain's capabilities
when: A capability has no position, position 0 or a repeated one; a use case has no capability or another domain's ID.
then: All are refused.

title: A use case under a capability, and everything under it, belongs to the capability's domain and counts in its coverage
when: A use case is moved under another capability of its domain.
then: Everything under a capability carries its domain and the pattern none; after the move the domain and the coverage are unchanged.

title: A repository persists exactly one aggregate, and an aggregate no repository persists is a gap
when: Loads a repository persisting one aggregate beside an aggregate no repository persists.
then: Expects an aggregate-without-repository gap for the unpersisted aggregate only, and no other problem.

title: Each Domain command changes one domain through its repository, held to its rules
when: Builds a domain with its own commands, changes its records and links, removes a domain service and a domain, then changes a repository to persist an aggregate another repository persists and adds a second repository persisting it, and runs domain commands from the CLI, the MCP tools and HTTP.
then: Expects each command to write only the Domain aggregate's tables, each removal referenced from outside refused naming the referrers, and both repository changes refused with one-repository, no file changed.

title: A repository that persists no aggregate is an error until its link is written
when: With a complete product that has no `repository-persists-nothing` error, removes every persists link of one repository.
then: Expects one `repository-persists-nothing` error naming that repository, and its aggregate an aggregate-without-repository gap.

title: A domain's services, which its commands and queries call, and its terms sit under the domain
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: Expects a read model under its domain with `read_model_field` parts and `reads` to an aggregate, a query under its read model, a domain service and a term under their domain (a term requiring `meaning`), `calls` from a command, a query or a read model to a domain service, each described in the reference in the domain-model stage, and the example's `EX-LEND-RM01` reads `EX-LEND-A2`, `EX-LEND-CMD01` calls `EX-LEND-DS01` and `EX-LEND-QRY01` sits under `EX-LEND-RM01`.

title: The migrations are numbered in order and recorded as applied
when: Applies the migrations to a fresh database.
then: Expects them numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on, each recorded with its name.

title: The schema read back loads each stored table after the tables it points at
when: Reads the schema's load order and foreign keys.
then: Expects every stored table a foreign key points at to come before it.

title: Removing a product kind while a record of it is left is refused
when: Opens a store whose product declares the kind `memo` under a domain and holds the record EX-LEND-M01 of it, then removes the `memo` product kind.
then: Expects the removal refused, naming `memo`.

title: The row types in src/store/tables.ts match the schema
when: Renders the row types from the schema description.
then: Expects them to equal the committed `lathe/src/platform/data/tables.ts`.

title: Every kind has an ID in the registry, a title and its parent columns
when: Reads every kind's table and parents from the schema description.
then: Expects each kind's table keyed by `id`, with a foreign key from `id` into `record_id`, a required title and a foreign key for each parent column; a lone parent column required, and two or three parent columns all optional with a CHECK that exactly one is given.

title: Each relation's pairs fit its link table's ends
when: Reads every relation's pairs and every supertype's members from the schema description.
then: Expects every relation to have pairs, each pair's kinds accepted by the link table's ends or their supertypes, and every supertype member a kind.

title: The server has no way to change the meta-model
when: Sends POST and PUT requests to `/api/spec` and to schema-like paths, and a write to a meta table, on the running server.
then: Expects them refused, and the migrations unchanged.

title: Which kinds are obligations, and which links design or prove a product's own obligation, come from the schema
when: Loads a product with its own obligation kind, with a design relation, a proof relation and one with no role.
then: Coverage lists exactly the kinds flagged as obligations; a record reached by the design and proof relations is designed and proved, one reached only by the relation with no role is neither.

title: Each kind the schema flags as an obligation is a member of the obligation supertype, and only those
when: Reads the schema's kinds and supertypes.
then: Expects the obligation supertype to be exactly Lathe's ten obligation kinds.

title: The schema describes every table and every column of a stored table
when: Reads every table and column in the schema description.
then: Expects a description on every table, and on every column of a stored table that is not a link table.

title: The schema version is one whole number in schema/version.json, and each converter moves the data forward one version
when: Reads schema/version.json and Lathe's own converters, then a folder of converters with one that skips a version.
then: Expects SCHEMA_VERSION to be the file's number, Lathe's converters to chain from 1 to it one version each, and a converter that skips a version refused.

title: 1-to-2 puts every flow through its product's one new interface, renaming its flows, steps and tests wherever they are named
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter on a committed product at schema 1 with a flow, its step and test, a fulfills link and a requirement whose text names the step.
then: Every ID and mention ends in FL01, the flow goes through the new TL-IF01, and the to-dos say what is left.

title: 1-to-2 gives every test one of the five levels, and a manual test the level that fits its kind
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of each test kind at the seven old levels, manual among them.
then: database becomes integration, api and contract service, e2e-api system, e2e-ui browser; a manual flow, view, use case or policy test browser, any other the lowest level its kind allows, with a to-do to check it.

title: 1-to-2 puts every repository under its aggregate's domain, persisting that aggregate, renamed wherever it is named
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of repositories under their aggregates, in two domains, one named by a link, a part and a text.
then: Each repository sits under its aggregate's domain as <domain>-REPO<nn>, numbered in its aggregates' order, with a persists link to its one aggregate; the link, the part and the text name the new ID, and the to-dos say to split a class that persists several aggregates into one repository each, and to rename the IDs in code.

title: 1-to-2 drops the descriptions that are gone, opens each When with its Given, and stands in for each required text a record lacks
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of two commands (one without a description), a data model with a description, a flow step, and two invariant tests with a Given, one without a When.
then: Expects the data model's description gone and the step with none, each Given opening its test's When (or becoming it), the command without a description given "To write: what it changes and when it is refused.", the three changes counted, and one to-do naming TL-LEND-CMD02's description.

title: 1-to-2 puts each command under its aggregate's root entity, and leaves a to-do for an aggregate with none
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on a command of an aggregate with a root entity and one of an aggregate with none.
then: Expects the first under the root entity (entity_id in place of aggregate_id), the second left as it was with a to-do naming it, and the to-do to move commands that change a child entity.

title: 1-to-2 drops every recorded exception and waiver, and leaves a to-do to change the model
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of a command change, a repository share, a pattern rule with its setting and applies-when condition, and a setting value with a not-applicable reason.
then: The command change and the repository share are gone, the rule keeps only its own columns, the reason is the setting's value, and the to-dos name each one to change in the model.

title: Each test is of the test kind named after what it tests, and sits under that one record, which it proves
when: A use case test is removed, or written under another requirement.
then: Each test kind has one required parent named by its kind; only that requirement goes unproved.

title: A declared product kind and its record load on the next load, placed under its domain
when: Loads a product that declares the kind `memo` under a domain, at stage `use-cases`, with its record EX-LEND-M01 under EX-LEND.
then: Expects `memo` listed last with stage `use-cases`, no position and parent kind `domain`, EX-LEND-M01 placed under EX-LEND in domain EX-LEND, and no problems.

title: A product kind and relation are declared, changed and removed through the Product aggregate
when: Declares a product kind with its fields and a relation, adds a record of the kind, changes the fields, then removes the kind with records and without.
then: Expects the kind's table to follow each declaration, and a kind still holding records to be refused at the commit.

title: Each Extension record command changes one record of a product kind, held to its declaration
when: Adds and changes records of a product kind with their fields, links and packages, and gives a field, relation or kind the declaration lacks.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the aggregate's tables, and each refused one to name its rule and leave every data file as it was.

title: An extension record goes with its links and packages, refused while referenced
when: Removes a record with the links it starts and the packages it names, then one a record of another kind sits under.
then: Expects the removal to take its rows, and the referenced one to be refused, naming the referrer.

title: The CLI, the MCP tools and HTTP each run the Extension record command they name
when: Runs Extension record commands and queries as lathe extension-record, as MCP tools and as POST /api/extension-record/<command>.
then: Expects each to run the one command it names, and a refusal to give every reason.

title: A product's own kind is listed after Lathe's, with its own label, stage and obligation, and Lathe's kinds keep theirs
when: Loads a product with its own kind in the domain model.
then: The product's kind comes after Lathe's, with its own label, stage, parent and obligation; Lathe's kinds are as in a product with no kinds of its own.

title: A product relation with a new name gets a link table of its own; one with Lathe's name adds only its pair
when: Loads a product that declares a pair for Lathe's `about` and a relation of its own.
then: `about` gains only the new pair and Lathe's other relations are unchanged; the product's relation gets its own link table.

title: A kind declared twice is refused, naming its file and line and the line of the first
when: The same product kind is declared twice.
then: A primary-key refusal on line 2 of the declaration file, naming the kind and line 1.

title: A product relation declared twice is refused once
when: Loads a product relation written twice in its file.
then: Expects one primary-key refusal naming data/product_relation.jsonl, line 2.

title: A pattern sits under the product with its settings, and use cases or domains follow it
when: A domain follows the pattern; a requirement tries to.
then: The domain loads with no pattern problem; the requirement is refused.

title: Each Pattern command changes one pattern through its repository, its settings given in order
when: Builds a pattern with its settings, a rule and a rule test with its own commands, replaces its settings, removes a rule, then removes a followed pattern and drops a setting a rule depends on, and runs its commands from the CLI and the MCP tools.
then: Expects the settings saved in the order given, a rule removed with its tests, and the removal of the followed pattern and of the depended-on setting refused, nothing changed.

title: A pattern rule is owed by each domain that follows its pattern, itself or through a use case, and proved there by one pattern rule test
when: Loads one domain that follows a pattern through a use case and has its rule test, and another that follows it itself with none.
then: The rule is owed in both and proved only in the first; a second test for one rule and domain is refused; a test naming a non-follower is an error.

title: A use case has one flow per interface, whose steps need a path and a position, fulfill its requirements, invoke a command or query, happen in a view and exchange with integrations
when: Reads the schema and loads the complete product.
then: Expects an interface under its product with a required kind of web app, API, CLI, agent tools, desktop or other; a flow under its use case with a required interface, unique per use case and interface; steps under their flow needing a path and a position, unique together; and steps loaded with their fulfills, invokes, happens_in and exchanges_with links.

title: A well-formed flow raises no step problem; a second flow through one interface, a repeated position, a step fulfilling another use case and a second invoke are refused
when: With a well-formed flow, writes a second flow through its interface, a repeated position, a step fulfilling another use case and a second invoke.
then: No step-order problem on the good flow; each broken row is refused.

title: A UC requirement no step of its flow fulfills is reported as not designed
when: The only fulfills link to a requirement is removed.
then: A designed gap and a not-designed warning, for that requirement only.

title: A UC requirement is designed only once a step of every flow of its use case fulfills it
when: Adds a second flow of a use case, through a CLI, whose one step fulfills nothing, then links that step to the requirement.
then: Its requirement is not designed, naming the second flow, until that flow's step fulfills it.

title: A flow's ID is its use case's ID, FL and its interface's number, and its interface is of its own product
when: A flow through a second interface is added with the right ID, a wrong one, and through another product's interface.
then: The first is accepted; flow-id-interface refuses the second and reference-crosses-product the third.

title: A step of a flow through an API, a CLI or agent tools happens in no view
when: With a step that happens in a view, makes its flow's interface each kind in turn.
then: step-fits-interface refuses it for API, CLI and agent tools, and accepts it for web app, desktop and other.

title: a step of an API flow that invokes what no endpoint exposes is reported, on the step
when: Makes the complete product's interface an API, with its steps in no view.
then: step-without-endpoint warns of each step whose command or query no endpoint exposes.

title: a flow test at a level its flow's interface does not fit is reported, manual or automated
when: Makes the complete product's interface an API, with one automated and one manual flow test at browser, then puts both at system, then makes the interface of kind other.
then: flow-test-level-for-interface warns of both at browser and of neither at system; an interface of kind other leaves them be.

title: An interface no flow goes through is a gap
when: Adds a second interface that no flow goes through.
then: An interface-without-flow gap names it.

title: Each use case command changes one use case through its repository and is refused, changing nothing, when it breaks a rule
when: Runs each kind of Use case command on a store: adds, changes, moves, links a step, and gives inputs that break a rule, an unknown field, a missing one or a write to another table.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the Use case aggregate's tables, and each refused one to name its rule and reason and leave every data file as it was.

title: Only repositories write data files, a handler loads only its own aggregate, and each command record names its handler's file
when: Reads every source file's imports, and every command definition beside Lathe's own command, handler, endpoint and CLI records.
then: Expects only repositories to import data-files.ts, only command handlers to import repositories and each only its own aggregate's, and every command definition to match its records one to one.

title: A use case goes whole, and a record referenced from outside what goes stays
when: Removes a use case with a requirement, flow and step, then a use case another aggregate follows and asks about, a requirement a step fulfills, a flow with its steps and a test a business outcome is measured by.
then: Expects the first use case and its flow to go with everything under them, and every other removal to be refused, naming each referrer.

title: The CLI, the MCP tools and HTTP each run the use case command they name
when: Runs use case commands and queries as lathe use-case with flags and JSON, as their MCP tools and as POST /api/use-case/<command>.
then: Expects each to change or read what it names, a refusal to give its reasons (exit 1, isError, 422), and an input of another shape to be refused before anything is read (exit 2, 400).

title: Each use case query is read by name over HTTP
when: Reads GET /api/use-case/get-use-case, next-id and list-use-cases over HTTP, with inputs of another shape, a record of another aggregate and a POST.
then: Expects each query on its own route beside the commands, the use case whole by the ID of any record in it, 400 for an input of another shape, 422 for a record it does not read, and 405 for a write.

title: A use case with no flow is a coverage gap, never an error
when: Loads a use case with no flow.
then: Expects a use-case-without-flow gap in its domain, and no error.

title: Requirements and rules may name a group, a column whose renaming changes no ID
when: A group is set on each of the five kinds, then renamed.
then: group_name is optional on all five; no ID changes and the renamed group loads.

title: A path whose positions skip a number is reported once, on the first step after the gap
when: Loads two steps of one flow on one path, written `refused` and `Refused`, at positions 2 and 3 with no step at 1.
then: Expects one `step-order` error, on the step at position 2.

title: The engine loads the six stages in order and each kind's stage and position, with the product and open questions outside them
when: A product is loaded.
then: Expects six stages in order, from Discovery to Test plan, each described; kind positions 1, 2, 3 running stage by stage; and only the product and the open question with no stage.

title: Every kind's stage is one of the schema's stages, and a product kind with no stage sits in none
when: Loads a product kind with no stage.
then: Every kind's stage is one of the schema's; the product kind has no stage and no position; the stages are unchanged.

title: The schema orders the stages, and the kinds stage by stage with the product first and open questions last
when: Reads the schema's stages and kinds.
then: Expects the six stages in order, and kind positions 1, 2, 3 running stage by stage from the product to the open question.

title: A product places its own kind in one of the six stages, or none, and cannot add a stage or change one of Lathe's kinds
when: Declares a product kind in each of the six stages, in none, in a stage that does not exist, and with the name of one of Lathe's kinds.
then: Each stage and no stage load and the stages are unchanged; the unknown stage and Lathe's name are refused.

title: Reads kinds, folders and relations from the schema, kinds in the schema's order
when: Builds the app's workspace from a product's schema description.
then: Expects kinds in the schema's kind positions, from product, business outcome and domain to question; the UC requirement's label, stage, parent, obligation, ID scope and required `statement`; the endpoint's two parents and the view's none; the six stages in order; and the `fulfills` relation with its design role and label.

title: The meta model read gives the kinds in the schema's reading order, the stages, the relations' words and each table's columns
when: Reads get-meta-model over two products' data.
then: Expects the product first and kinds by position, each with its stage, parents and ID scope; the six stages in order; each relation pair with its words from both ends; and every non-link table's columns.

title: An entity sits under an aggregate and needs a role, a value object has no owner, and entities link to entities by has_one and has_many
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: An entity sits under an aggregate with a required role, a value object has no owner and its constraints sit under it, the four field tables are parts, and has_one and has_many join entities, all described.

title: A well-formed domain model gives no entity problem, and each entity rule fails on its own data
when: With a well-formed domain model, leaves a child unreached, links across aggregates, adds a second root, drops a role and links an entity to itself.
then: No problems on the good model; entity-unreferenced, has-crosses-aggregate and refusals for the rest.

title: An entity's fields are its entity_field rows in position order, each with a name, a meaning, exactly one type and whether it is required
when: Loads entity fields written out of position order.
then: The fields come back by position with name, meaning, type and required, and an optional column name and example; only entities have entity fields; a field with no type or two is refused.

title: An entity, event or read model with no fields is a coverage gap
when: Loads an entity, an event and a read model with no fields.
then: Each is a coverage gap.

title: Another aggregate is referenced by a field typed by it: a foreign key in its own domain, a plain ID from another domain
when: With an entity whose field is typed by another domain's aggregate, adds foreign keys within the domain and into the other domain.
then: The field and the same-domain key load; the cross-domain key is refused; a has_many into another aggregate is an error.

title: Uniqueness is an invariant that a unique key may name and back up, built only by its rule, and only a unique key may name one
when: With an invariant a unique key names, whose rule's file is missing, then present; then a primary key and an index naming the invariant.
then: The invariant is not built through the key, then built through its rule; a primary key or index naming an invariant is refused.

title: Each Aggregate command changes one aggregate through its repository, and each interface runs the command it names
when: Builds the Aggregate aggregate's data set with its own Add commands, changes each kind, gives inputs of another shape, and runs commands as lathe aggregate with flags, as their MCP tools and as POST /api/aggregate/<command>.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the aggregate's own tables, each refused one to name its rule and reason, and each interface to run the command it names.

title: A child entity its root does not reach by has_one or has_many is a warning
when: Removes every `has_one` link of the complete product, leaving a child entity its root does not reach.
then: Expects one `entity-unreferenced` warning, on that child.

title: The Markdown gives the data model, then kinds with their tables, other tables, relations, folders and checks, each with an anchor
when: Renders Lathe's reference as Markdown.
then: Expects `# Lathe reference` first, then the data files, each stage from Domain model to Test plan with its kinds, checks and coverage gaps, Outside the stages with the open question, then Other tables, Relations and Checks of any kind; anchors for a stage, a kind, a table, a part table, a relation, a check and a gap; and more than 100 links inside the document, each landing on an anchor.

title: The reference script prints a product's reference, or writes it with --out
when: Runs the reference script for a product with its own kinds, with `--print` and with `--out`.
then: Expects the rendered reference in both.

title: The reference holds every kind, table, relation, folder and check of Lathe's schema
when: Builds Lathe's reference.
then: Expects the six stages in order, a use case's label, stage, parent, ID scope, ID pattern and children, the ten obligation kinds with their coverage and test kinds with their levels, each kind's table with its columns and references, a part table, a relation's pairs and role, every check row in run order, the engine's own `data-refused` and every gap rule.

title: A product's reference shows its own kinds and relations and its own checks
when: Builds the reference for a product with its own kind, relation and checks.
then: Expects a product's own kind with its table and relation pair, and its own checks after Lathe's.

title: The committed REFERENCE.md is the reference as the reference script writes it
when: Renders Lathe's reference.
then: Expects it to equal the committed `lathe/REFERENCE.md`.

title: A product's own checks are held to the same rule, and Lathe's are all documented
when: Reads Lathe's reference, and the reference of a product with checks of its own.
then: Expects every kind, table and check of Lathe's described, and a product's own checks with their summary and explanation.

title: The reference reads each relation by its labels
when: Builds the default reference.
then: Expects `fulfills` to carry the labels Fulfills and Fulfilled by, the relation's entry to read `Reads: Fulfills / Fulfilled by`, and the UC requirement's entry to list `Fulfilled by` under Links in.

title: A domain event sits under an aggregate, a command under the entity it changes raises and checks, and a policy under a command hears one event
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: Events, commands with raises and checks, and policies hearing one event are in the schema and described.

title: A command changes only its own aggregate, the one of the entity it sits under, and the schema keeps no way to record another
when: Loads commands under entities of their aggregates, and reads the schema's tables.
then: Each command counts for the aggregate of the entity it sits under, and no table records another aggregate a command changes.

title: Each Command command changes one command through its repository, and each interface runs the command it names
when: Builds the Command aggregate's data set with its own Add commands, changes each kind, gives inputs of another shape, and runs commands as lathe command with flags, as their MCP tools and as POST /api/command/<command>.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the aggregate's own tables, each refused one to name its rule and reason, and each interface to run the command it names.

title: A test data set sits under a domain, and any kind of test starts from any number of them
when: Adds a second data set, links two kinds of test to data sets, links a use case to one, and names a data set for another domain.
then: Every test kind and only a test starts from a data set; the use case's link is refused, and so is the misnamed ID.

title: Each Test data set command changes one test data set through its repository, and one a test starts from stays
when: Adds, changes, reads and removes a test data set with its own commands, then removes one a test starts from, and runs its commands from the CLI and the MCP tools.
then: Expects each command to write only the test_data_set table, its domain never to change, and the removal of the used one refused naming the test that starts from it.

title: A data set no test starts from is an error; a missing file is an error when an automated test starts from it, else a warning
when: Unlinks every test from the complete product's data set, removes its seed file, makes its one test not automated yet, and names a folder of fixtures.
then: test-data-set-unused is an error; test-data-set-file-missing is an error, then a warning; a folder gives no problem.

title: A kind and a check open from where the Reader meets them
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reading a record opens its kind, a column and a problem code and lands on the format page each time, without leaving the workbench.
when: Open a record's page; choose its kind in the wiki card, a column's label, and a problem's code.
then: Each opens its kind or check page in the same workbench, one step each.

title: A standard sits under the product, its rules under it and their tests under each rule, and technical records meet a rule
when: Reads the schema and the reference; adds a `meets` link from a UC requirement and from an invariant test to `TL-STD-CODE-R01`, and one from a command handler to the missing `TL-STD-CODE-R09`.
then:
Expects a standard under the product (`

-STD-`), a standard rule under its standard (`-R`, an obligation) and a standard rule test under its rule (`-T`, test plan, levels unit to browser); `meets` labeled Meets and Met by, from every technical kind to a standard rule; all three described in the reference; and the three links refused, the last as `foreign-key` at `data/meets.jsonl` line 1.

title: Each Standard command changes one standard through its repository, and a rule a technical record meets stays
when: Builds a standard with a rule and its test with its own commands, reads it, removes it whole, then removes a rule a command handler meets, and runs its commands from the MCP tools.
then: Expects the standard removed with its rules and tests, and the removal of the met rule refused naming the command handler that meets it.

title: A standard rule is owed by the product, designed and built by the technical records that meet it and proved by its standard rule tests
when: With a standard rule met by a technical record and proved by a standard rule test, removes its test, marks it not automated yet, or points it at a file that does not name it.
then: The rule counts outside every domain; without a valid test it is designed and built but not proved, and a test not automated yet is counted as such.

title: A standard rule that nothing meets is reported as not designed, not built and not proved; naming it in text does not meet it
when: Loads a standard rule named only in a UI component's description.
then: The rule is not designed and not proved, with a not-proved warning; no meets link exists.

title: A standard rule with no standard rule test is designed and built but not proved
when: Loads a product whose standard rule is met by a technical record with a file and has no test.
then: Expects it designed and built, and not proved.

title: A technical record sits under the one design record it implements and names its file; a file not there yet is work to do
when: Reads each technical kind's parents from the schema; adds a second command handler `TL-LEND-CMD01-H2` for one command; loads the complete product with `src/dates.ts` missing.
then: Expects each technical kind but the UI component and the repository to sit under one design record, unique per parent, and a table under an entity, a read model or a domain; the second handler refused as `unique`; and a `technical-file-missing` warning, 'Service EX-LEND-DS01-SV names src/dates.ts, which does not exist yet.', with the gap `built EX-LEND-DS01`.

title: A technical record whose file does not exist is a warning; a folder will do
when: Loads technical records naming a missing file, a missing folder and a folder that exists.
then: Expects a technical-file-missing warning for each missing one, and nothing for the folder.
