then: Every command runs from its key and from the palette, the screen reader announces what changed, typing in a search box never fires a single-key shortcut, and the overridden binding runs its command after a reload and shows in the shortcuts sheet.

title: The Reader learns a shortcut where it is used
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: Rest on a control that has a shortcut, open the palette and the shortcuts sheet, and reach the control with a screen reader; then override its binding and look again.
then: The tooltip, the palette, the shortcuts sheet and the screen reader (`aria-keyshortcuts`) each give the same keys, and after the override each gives the new keys.

title: The Reader arranges the workbench and it stays so
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: Drag and key-step the gap between two panels and double-click it, drag the navigation small, collapse the wiki card and bring it back, then reload.
then: The panels resize by drag and by arrow keys, a double-click resets the gap to its default, the navigation hides when dragged small, the wiki card collapses and comes back, and after the reload every panel is as it was left.

title: The Reader chooses or makes a theme for the whole app
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: Press g then t, arrow through the themes and keep one; switch Light, Dark and System from the palette; in Appearance duplicate a theme, edit, reset, export and delete it, and import the exported file.
then: The chosen theme and mode apply to the whole app at once and survive a reload; the duplicate edits, resets, exports as a JSON file and deletes; and importing the file adds it back as a theme of the Reader's own.

title: The Reader reads and moves around Lathe on a phone
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: On a phone, open Lathe, search for a use case by its ID, switch to the Graph, pinch and open a node, use the wiki card sheet, the nav sheet and the Open pages sheet; then use a tablet in landscape.
then: Text is readable without zooming, every target is large enough for a finger, no page scrolls sideways, the search opens the use case, the graph pans and pinches and opens the node, and each sheet opens and closes; on the tablet the panels show side by side.

title: Nothing the Reader is looking at jumps
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: Open a page; move between records by the nav, a link, the graph, Back and quick find; collapse and resize the wiki card and the panels, fold rows, move around the graph and the ERD; reload while scrolled; open a tooltip and the overlays; switch the theme; and on a phone open and close the sheets.
then: Nothing on screen moves unless the Reader moved it: the nav, the page bar and the header strip stay put, the reload comes back at the same scroll, and the tooltip, overlays and sheets open where they show without pushing the page.

title: The Reader uses Lathe by keyboard and screen reader
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: With a screen reader on and only the keyboard, tab round the nav, the tab panel, the wiki card and the stage, open records, switch stages and collapse the wiki card, pick High contrast in light and dark, and open a dialog and a phone sheet.
then: Every control is reached by Tab in order with a visible focus ring and announced by its name and state, records open and stages switch from the keyboard, High contrast passes in light and dark, and focus moves into the dialog and the sheet and returns when they close.

title: Open Product Folder opens the chosen folder in its own window and refuses a folder that is no product
manual_reason: Manual because it watches what only a person at the screen sees: a flash, the Dock and real windows. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`.
when: In the desktop app (`npm --prefix desktop start`), presses Cmd+O and chooses a folder with neither `lathe.config.json` nor `data/`, then chooses another product's folder.
then: The first is refused with a message saying what is missing and no window opens; the second opens in a window of its own.

title: The desktop window's title names the product and its folder
when: Runs the real shell, hidden, on a product folder named Smoke Shop and reads the page's text and the window's title.
then: Expects the page's text to contain `Smoke Shop` and the window's title to be `Smoke Shop — <the folder, with ~ for the home folder>`.
notes: T106's title from the product rows (unit); PO01's and PO03's effects seen in the same run

title: A new window opens on the shell color with no white flash
manual_reason: Manual because it watches what only a person at the screen sees: a flash, the Dock and real windows. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`.
when: Runs `npm --prefix desktop start` in light appearance, then in dark.
then: Lathe's repo opens in a window that shows the shell color at once, never a white flash.

title: The page in the desktop app has only window.latheDesktop's members, and no Node
when: Runs the real shell, hidden, on a small product folder and reads the members of `window.latheDesktop` in the page and whether Node is there.
then: Expects `window.latheDesktop` to have exactly `chat`, `copyRecordId`, `isDesktop`, `onAppRequest`, `onCommand`, `onFullScreen`, `openRecordInEditor`, `platform`, `revealRecord`, `setChrome`, `setErrorCount` and `showRecordMenu`, and no Node in the page.

title: A link to another site opens in the system browser, and the window stays on Lathe
manual_reason: Manual because it watches what only a person at the screen sees: a flash, the Dock and real windows. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`.
when: In the desktop app, clicks a link to an outside site in a record.
then: The site opens in the system browser, and the window stays on Lathe.

title: The desktop app quits cleanly, with exit code 0, while a reload is in progress
when: At the end of the smoke run, touches the product's data files and asks the window's server for the specs, then quits about 20 ms later.
then: Expects the reload to have still been in progress when the run quit, and the app to exit with code 0, not ended by an uncaught Napi::Error from the database engine.

title: A workspace folder opens with the data folder of each product it lists
when: Checks a workspace folder whose config lists a product folder with its own data folder, and one with no config.
then: Expects the workspace's data folder and the listed product's, and both products' names for the title; a listed folder with no config left for the server to report.

title: A product opens with its own installed Lathe when it has one, else the bundled copy, and About says which
when: Chooses the Lathe for a folder with no installed Lathe, one with a built one, and one with an unbuilt one, and builds the About model.
then: Expects the bundled copy, the product's own with its version, and the bundled copy again; and About's Opened with row only when a product is in front.

title: Open Recent, the next launch and a window's place
manual_reason: It takes the built app's menus and windows across launches: a person checks it.
when: Open two folders, move and resize a window, close it, reopen it from File › Open Recent, quit and launch again, then clear Open Recent.
then: Open Recent lists both, latest first, the window reopens where it was, the launch reopens the last folder, and Clear empties the list.

title: The desktop app loads the 5199 dev server when it serves the opened folder
manual_reason: Manual because it changes files while the shell runs and builds the app. Run it after changing `desktop/scripts/` or the servers.
when: With the dev server running (`npm --prefix app run dev`), runs `npm --prefix desktop run dev`, then changes a style in `app/src/styles.css`.
then: The terminal says Lathe's folder comes "from shared dev server at http://localhost:5199", and the window updates without reloading, as the browser does.
notes: SP02-T and INV06-T prove the choice at unit level

title: Without a 5199 server for the folder, the shell starts and loads a dev server of its own
manual_reason: Manual because it changes files while the shell runs and builds the app. Run it after changing `desktop/scripts/` or the servers.
when: With `npm --prefix desktop run dev` running, opens another product folder with Cmd+O.
then: The terminal says it comes "from own dev server" on a port other than 5199, and the window shows that product.

title: A change under desktop/src restarts Electron, and a failed build leaves the shell running
manual_reason: Manual because it changes files while the shell runs and builds the app. Run it after changing `desktop/scripts/` or the servers.
when: With `npm --prefix desktop run dev` running, changes a comment in `desktop/src/menu.ts`, then breaks the file's syntax.
then: The terminal says it restarts Electron and the windows come back; with the broken file the build fails and the running shell stays.

title: A change to the opened product's specs reloads the page in every server mode
manual_reason: Manual because it changes files while the shell runs and builds the app. Run it after changing `desktop/scripts/` or the servers.
when: Changes a record's title in an open product folder, on its page or with `lathe use-case change-use-case`, in a window of `npm --prefix desktop run dev` loading its own dev server, then in one of `npm --prefix desktop start`.
then: Each page shows the new title within a second or two.

title: A local pack builds an unsigned app for this Mac in desktop/release, and nothing is signed or published
manual_reason: Manual because it changes files while the shell runs and builds the app. Run it after changing `desktop/scripts/` or the servers.
when: Runs `npm --prefix desktop run pack` and opens the app it builds from Finder.
then: `desktop/release/mac-arm64/Lathe.app` (or `mac` on Intel) is built, the log says code signing was skipped, and the app opens with the chuck icon (right-click › Open the first time, since it is unsigned).

title: The page in the desktop app finds window.latheDesktop, so it knows it runs there
when: Runs the real shell, hidden, on a small product folder and reads `window.latheDesktop.isDesktop` in the page.
then: Expects `window.latheDesktop.isDesktop` to be true.

title: The menus run the page's commands
manual_reason: Only macOS shows the native menu bar: a person checks it in the built app.
when: Open the menu bar in the desktop app and choose View items that stand for the app's commands.
then: The menus are File, Edit, View, Window and Help, and each View item does what its key does in the page.

title: File › Open Records In offers the editors, checks the one in use and chooses another
when: Builds the File menu and chooses another editor in Open Records In.
then: Expects Cursor, Zed, the default app and a command of the Owner's own offered, the one in use checked, and the choice saved.

title: The Reader works under Lathe's own title bar
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: In the desktop app, go back and forward from the title bar, click the command center, show and hide the navigation, drag the bar and double-click it, then change the theme.
then: Back and forward move through the history, the command center opens quick find, the navigation hides and shows, dragging the bar moves the window and a double-click zooms it, and the bar follows the new theme with no flash.

title: A second launch or a folder opened from Finder goes to the running app
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: With the packed app running, runs `open -a Lathe ~/some/product` or drags a product folder onto the Dock icon, then does it again.
then: The running app opens the folder in a window, and the second time brings that window forward; no second app starts.
notes: T124 routes a second launch at unit level.

title: The window has no spell check, overlay scroll bars and native context menus, and reopens in full screen
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: In the desktop app, scrolls a long page, right-clicks in quick find, then enters full screen, quits and reopens.
then: The scroll bars float over the page, the right-click offers Cut, Copy and Paste, and the window comes back in full screen with the title bar's back button at the left edge.

title: A killed run leaves macOS no window state to offer to reopen
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: Force quits Lathe while it opens its window, then opens it again.
then: macOS does not offer to reopen windows; Lathe opens its own last folder.
notes: T127 (`desktop/test/persistence.test.ts`) checks the defaults at unit level.

title: The shell opts out of macOS window restoration, on a Mac and for a test harness's Electron
when: Starts the shell on macOS, elsewhere, and as a test harness runs the unpacked Electron.
then: Expects ApplePersistenceIgnoreState and NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows set on macOS and for the harness, and nothing elsewhere.

title: The Dock, the app menu and the error page behave as a Mac app's
manual_reason: Only macOS shows the Dock and the app menu: a person checks them in the built app.
when: Keep Lathe in the Dock with a folder that has check errors and one the engine cannot load; open the Dock menu, About Lathe and Settings…
then: The icon reads at every size, the badge counts the front window's errors, the Dock menu opens a folder and lists the recent ones, About shows the versions, Settings… opens Appearance, and the folder that cannot load opens the error page saying why.

title: Writes through the store and answers with the rows it changed
when: Posts a write the store accepts, adding a UC requirement, to the dev API plugin over a copy of a product, then asks for GET /api/spec.
then: Expects 200, `data/uc_requirement.jsonl` holding 'The note MUST be saved.', and `/api/spec` listing `EX-NOTE-UC01-R01`.

title: Refuses a write from another site, one not sent as JSON, and one that is not a list of commands
when: Posts writes with origin `https://elsewhere.example`, with `sec-fetch-site: cross-site`, with origin `http://127.0.0.1:5300`, and with content type `text/plain`.
then: Expects 403 for the other origin and the cross-site request, 200 for the local origin, and 415 for the plain text.

title: A product whose data is for another schema version stops every load with what to do
when: Loads a product whose config names no schema, then a newer one, and reads configs whose schema is not a whole number from 1.
then: Expects no schema read as 1; the newer one refused by loadConfig, loadWorkspace and openStore with the newer-Lathe message; the older message naming npx lathe upgrade; and the bad schemas refused.

title: The MCP server of a product for another schema offers only check, and every tool says what to do
when: Serves the MCP tools for a product whose config names a newer schema, and calls check and show.
then: Expects the instructions to start with the message, tools/list to hold only check, and both calls refused with the message and nothing changed.

title: Upgrade runs the converters in order on the raw rows, and raises the schema once the data loads
when: Upgrades a committed product from schema 1 to 3 with two converters given out of order: one renames a column the schema does not know, one adds a column.
then: Expects the converters run in order, the product row in the store's line format with both changes, the summary, schema 3 in the config, nothing to do a second time, and an older target refused.

title: Upgrade lists what it could not convert, and stops without raising the schema when the data no longer loads
when: Upgrades with a converter that leaves a to-do, one whose files phase leaves a column the schema refuses, and with a converter missing.
then: Expects the to-do listed and the schema raised; the refusal listed as a to-do with the schema unchanged; and the missing converter refused with nothing changed.

title: Upgrade refuses a working tree with changes, or no git
when: Upgrades a product with a file not committed, then once it is committed, then a product not under git.
then: Expects the first refused naming the changed file with the schema unchanged, the second upgraded, and the third refused as not in a git repository.

title: The MCP launcher warns once when the installed Lathe is not the major version the skills were written for
when: Starts the launcher for a product whose installed Lathe is one major version on, and for one at the skills' major version, and calls show twice in each.
then: Expects the manifest's major to be the package's, the warning with both versions and the schema in the first result only, and no warning at the same major version.

title: The launcher says why it cannot start outside a Lathe repo
when: Starts the launcher in a folder with no Lathe repo.
then: Expects it to exit saying why it cannot start.

title: Text with quotes, newlines and backticks given as JSON is written exactly, from stdin or a file, in the tool's shape
when: Adds a requirement from stdin and changes a use case's goal from a file with an aggregate command's `--json`, each with quotes, newlines, backticks, tabs and accents, then a flow step's list as JSON and the same command's tool. Pipes an add under a use case that does not exist as JSON and gives the same add as flags; pipes JSON with a field flag, text that does not parse, and names a JSON file that does not exist.
then: Expects the text read back exactly and the tool and the CLI to read one input one way; the same refusal as the flag form with the data files unchanged; and exit 2 with the reason for bad usage, nothing written.

title: No skill tells the Agent to write spec files by hand
when: Reads every skill of the plugin, with every tool name and every tool call example in it, and the product kinds and relations the examples declare.
then: Expects no skill to tell the Agent to edit data files, only to use the tools; every tool named to belong to one of Lathe's aggregates and to exist once that aggregate's commands have landed; each example's input to pass its tool's own input check, or, for an aggregate still to land, each field to be a column, relation or part of its kind, with values of the columns' types.

title: The chat runs the Owner's own Claude Code in the folder and continues its session
when: Drives a `ChatSession` against a stand-in CLI: sends a message on a new session; opens a saved session to resume, closes it and sends again; and opens one to fork.
then: Expects the answer streamed and completed, the session named by a UUID and the CLI run in the folder; the resume run with `--resume`, the saved items shown first, and the CLI started again on the same session after it ended; and the fork run with `--resume <id> --fork-session`, ending under a new session ID.

title: The chat runs the CLI headless, with structured input and output
when: Builds the CLI's arguments for a new, a resumed and a forked session, and writes a message, a permission answer and a stop as lines for the CLI.
then: Expects `-p` with stream-json input and output, verbose partial messages and `--permission-prompt-tool stdio`, plus `--resume` and `--fork-session` as asked; a user line with the text; a control response that allows with the tool's input unchanged, or denies; and an interrupt control request.

title: The chat finds the Owner's own claude
when: Looks for `claude` with a configured path, on the PATH and where the installers put it, and reads `claudePath` from the settings.
then: Expects the configured path when it exists and none when it does not; else the first `claude` on the PATH, else `~/.local/bin/claude`, else none; and the setting trimmed, an empty one left out.

title: The chat is offered in the desktop app on a wide window, and nowhere else
when: Opens a use case in a browser, with no desktop bridge, and in the desktop app on a phone-sized screen.
then: Expects no chat panel and no chat toggle in the browser, and no chat panel on the phone.

title: Record IDs in Claude's answers open the record on the stage
when: Pushes a question and an answer naming `DM-SHOP-CMD01` in bold and `NOPE-1` into the chat, then clicks the record's link.
then: Expects the answer drawn as Markdown, `DM-SHOP-CMD01` a link titled with its record's title and `NOPE-1` left as text, and the click opening the command's page on the stage.

title: Tool calls are rows that expand, and a turn's changed records show as diffs
when: Pushes a finished tool call and expands its row; pushes a running turn during which the data reloads with a command renamed, then its answer; and compares two indexes with one record removed, one added and one changed.
then: Expects the row closed until clicked, then its result and a done mark; the turn followed by "1 record changed" with the command's old title struck out and its new one inserted; and the removed, added and changed records found, the changed field with its before and after, and none between an index and itself.

title: The CLI's stream becomes the chat's text, tool rows and prompts
when: Feeds the CLI's stream lines into the chat's state: streamed then completed text, tool calls with their results, a subagent's text, a permission request and its cancel, turn results and unreadable lines; then diffs two states into patches.
then: Expects the text once, completed in place, and the session's ID; each tool call a row with its label and one-line summary, closed by its result or its error; a subagent's text kept out; the prompt pending, then withdrawn; the turn ended idle with an error notice or "Stopped."; unreadable lines ignored; and a patch of only the changed items, a reset when items are gone.

title: A permission prompt waits for the Owner, and Stop ends the turn
when: Asks the stand-in CLI for a tool that needs permission, then allows it, denies it, or stops the turn; and opens a session whose CLI does not exist.
then: Expects the prompt pending with the tool and its summary; once allowed, the answer recorded and the tool done, a second answer refused; once denied, the tool in error; on Stop, the chat stopping, then idle with the prompt withdrawn and "Stopped.", the next message going to the same process; and a CLI that cannot start closing the chat with an error notice.

title: The Owner answers a permission prompt in the chat and stops a turn
when: Pushes a pending permission prompt and answers Allow once, then Deny; sends a message with Enter and stops the turn with the Stop button and with Escape; and walks the messages with the arrow keys, Home and End.
then: Expects the prompt naming the tool and what it would do, each answer sent to the shell and, once answered, "Allowed once" with no buttons; the message sent, "Claude is working…" shown and two stops sent; and focus moving between the messages, only the last in the tab order.

title: The picker lists the folder's saved sessions by title and date, and warns of one open elsewhere
when: Names the session store's folder for a product folder, titles sessions from their transcripts' ends, lists a folder's transcripts with one running elsewhere, reads the registry of running sessions, and finds transcripts by session ID.
then: Expects the folder named as the CLI names it; a title from the custom title, else the summary, else the first real prompt, cut to 80 characters; sessions newest first, empty ones left out, marked running or just written; only other processes' live sessions from the registry; and only a session ID's own transcript found, a path or an unknown ID refused.

title: The picker resumes, forks or starts a session, and warns of one open elsewhere
when: Opens the chat's session picker and resumes, forks and starts sessions; picks a session open in another client; opens the picker with no Claude Code found; and dates sessions.
then: Expects the sessions by title and age, the busy one marked "Open elsewhere"; resume, fork and new sent to the shell; for the busy one, a warning offering Fork instead and nothing opened until it is chosen; with no Claude Code, a message saying how to set it up and New session disabled; and dates as "this minute", "3 hours ago", "yesterday" or the date.

title: A resumed session shows its saved conversation
when: Reads a saved transcript with prompts, meta and command lines, text, tool calls with and without results, a subagent's line and a broken line; then one longer than the limit.
then: Expects the main thread's prompt, text and tool calls, a tool call with no saved result in error, and the rest skipped; and for the long one, only the last `TRANSCRIPT_LIMIT` items after a notice of how many earlier items the transcript holds.

title: Claude asks what the Reader is looking at and opens a record, only with an app window connected
when: Lists the MCP server's tools with and without an app bridge, reads the bridge from the environment, and calls `app_focus` and `app_open` through a stand-in bridge, then with none, a closed window, an unreachable bridge and a wrong token.
then: Expects `app_focus` and `app_open` listed only with a bridge; the bridge read only for a local address with its token; the focus named by ID, kind, title and stage with the selection, product and page; a record opened, a refusal passed on as an error and a bad stage refused; and "No Lathe app window is connected" in every other case.

title: The app bridge answers for its window, and only with its token
when: Starts the app bridge and calls a window's focus and open routes with and without its token, a closed window's and an unknown route, and checks open requests.
then: Expects a 127.0.0.1 address per window with a 48-hex-digit token; the window's focus, and 404 for a closed window; the record opened with the window's answer passed on, a bad ID 400; 401 for a wrong token, 405 for a GET to open and 404 for another route; and an open request with an ID and a known stage or none accepted, others refused.

title: The page answers the app bridge: what the Reader is looking at, and opening a record
when: Opens a use case on the ERD stage and answers the bridge's focus question, then opens a command on the Graph stage and a record that does not exist.
then: Expects the focus named by ID, kind and title with its stage and product and nothing selected; the command opened at its address with a message naming it and the stage; and a refusal saying there is no such record in this window's specs.

title: lathe app focus and lathe app open reach the window as the app tools do, and refuse with none
when: Runs lathe app focus and lathe app open against a stand-in bridge, against a closed window and with none.
then: Expects the text and JSON app_focus and app_open give, the record opened on the stage given, a refusal with exit 1 when no window is connected, and exit 2 for bad usage.

title: Coverage counts an obligation designed once its design is specified
when: Leaves one UC requirement with no step that fulfills it, and one standard rule with no technical record that meets it.
then: Expects exactly those two counted as not designed, and every other obligation counted designed by construction.

title: The coverage read gives each scope's figures, tests by state and gaps, the product's own scope first
when: Reads get-coverage for one of two products over a checks' run.
then: Expects the product's own scope then each domain's, each with its obligation figures, tests by state and gaps, nothing of the other product.

title: Coverage counts satisfied and proved requirements and lists the gaps
when: Loads the complete product with one step of `EX-LEND-UC02-FL01` no longer fulfilling its requirement, the specification's test not automated yet and `src/dates.ts` missing.
then: Expects not-designed to say "UC requirement EX-LEND-UC02-R01 is not designed yet: no step of EX-LEND-UC02-FL01 fulfills it.", not-built to name `EX-LEND-DS01`, and not-proved to say "Specification EX-LEND-SP01 is not proved yet: its test is not automated yet."

title: An automated test whose file does not name it leaves its obligation unproved, listed as a gap
when: Loads the complete product with the policy test's file not naming the test.
then: Expects the policy listed as a gap, not proved yet.

title: Coverage gaps are warnings, so an unfinished design has no errors
when: Loads the complete product with one step of `EX-LEND-UC02-FL01` no longer fulfilling its requirement, the specification's test not automated yet and `src/dates.ts` missing.
then: Expects not-designed, not-built and not-proved each to report, as warnings, exactly the obligations coverage lists as not designed, not built and not proved, with the same messages.

title: Coverage counts designed, built and proved separately
when: Removes the value types, predicates, event handlers, endpoint handlers and builds links, and leaves the domain service's file unwritten.
then: Expects each obligation whose technical record is missing, or names no file that exists, counted as not built, apart from designed and proved.

title: An invariant is built only by its rule, once the rule's file exists: no data model or unique key builds it
when: Loads a product whose invariant has no rule though its aggregate's data models name files and a unique key names it, then the complete product, then that with the rule's file missing.
then: Expects it not built, then built, then not built.

title: A UC requirement is built only through the handler of what its steps invoke: a UI component of the view a step happens in builds nothing
when: Loads a product whose only fulfilling step invokes nothing but happens in a rendered view, then one where a second step invokes a query.
then: Expects a built gap naming the requirement, then the requirement built.

title: Each record short of a minimum is a gap under its own scope, named by its rule
when: Loads a product short of every minimum, the complete product, and an entity kept in its root's table.
then: Expects a gap of every rule under its scope and no problem for any, none on the complete product, no table asked of the entity in its root's table, and every rule with a unique name, a stage and a summary.

title: Coverage counts every obligation kind in meta-model order, including interaction requirements
when: Loads the complete product.
then: Expects coverage for `EX-LEND` and for the product's Shared; the obligation kinds in kind order from constraint to standard rule; two UC requirements and one of each other kind covered in `EX-LEND`, a pattern rule counted for proof only; the constraint and view requirement in the domain that uses them, the standard rule only in Shared; and no gaps.

title: An extension's obligation kind and design and proof relations are counted like the defaults
when: Loads a product that declares a `house_rule` obligation kind with two rules, a `script` kind whose `enforces` design relation designs one rule, and a `checks_rule` proof relation from a use case test to that rule.
then: Expects `house_rule` labeled House rule with a total of 2, and 1 designed, 1 built and 1 proved.

title: An obligation is built only when every record that implements it names a file that exists, a UC requirement through what its commands check and call
when: Loads the complete product with one of the two handler files missing; then without the predicate of the specification the command checks; then with the file of the service it calls missing; then with one entity's data model naming a file that does not exist; then with a second UI component building the view requirement, its file written and then missing.
then: The UC requirement counts as not built each time, though a handler's file exists; the invariant still counts as built, as only its rule builds it; the view requirement is built while both builders' files exist and not built once one is missing.

title: Only automated and manual tests prove; a test not automated yet leaves its obligation unproved
when: Loads the complete product with the constraint test at `service`, the specification test not automated yet, the view test manual, no standard rule test, and the policy test's file not naming it.
then: Expects `proved` gaps on exactly `EX-LEND-PO01`, `EX-LEND-SP01`, `EX-STD-CODE-R01` and `EX-VO01-C01`, and the view requirement covered by its manual test.

title: The check prints one coverage line per domain and obligation kind, with not-automated-yet counts
when: Runs lathe check on the complete product with one test not automated yet and one file missing, and on a sparse product.
then: Expects one coverage line per domain and obligation kind with designed, built, proved and not-automated-yet counts and their gaps, and the records short of a minimum.

title: The meta-model's obligation and role columns are loaded into the workspace
when: Loads a product that declares a `house_rule` kind as an obligation and a `script` kind that is not.
then: Expects `house_rule` loaded as an obligation and `script` not, `house_rule` counted last in the domain's coverage after Lathe's kinds, and `script` not counted.

title: A view requirement is built only by a UI component that builds it, not by one that only renders its view
when: Loads the complete product, then the same without its builds links, then with the building component's file missing.
then: Expects the view requirement built at first, then not built and the component that only renders its view untraced, then not built.

title: Proof counts only at a level the test's kind allows
when: Loads the complete product with its constraint test run at `service`, a level a constraint test does not allow.
then: Expects the constraint counted in its domain but not proved, and listed there as a `proved` gap.

title: A constraint counts in its value object's domain, or in Shared when two domains use it
when: Loads the complete product, then adds a second domain whose entity has a field typed by the constraint's value object.
then: Expects the constraint counted in Lending, whose entity alone uses its value object; then, with a second domain's entity field typed by it too, counted once in Shared and in neither domain.

title: A product kind that names a file proves a rule only while the file names it
when: Proves three house rules: one by a use case test, one by a product kind that names a file, and one by a product kind that names no file; then loads the product again with that file leaving the ID out.
then: Expects all three proved at first, and then two: the rule whose file leaves the ID out is no longer proved, and the one with no file still is.

title: A step exchanging with an integration is built by its adapter; a product kind's record under it builds nothing
when: A UC requirement's only fulfilling step invokes nothing, happens in no view and exchanges with an integration; then the adapter's file is missing; then the adapter is gone and a plugin hook of a product kind under the integration names a file.
then: Expects it built through the adapter, then not built, then still not built through the hook, and not built when the step exchanges with nothing.

title: A business outcome no capability serves, and a capability that serves no outcome, are coverage gaps
when: Removes the complete product's serves link.
then: The outcome's gap is the product's, the capability's its domain's, and no problem is reported.

title: A source file no technical record names is a gap; tests, configs, generated files and build output are left out
when: With a product whose records name one file and one folder, and other source files, tests, configs, a generated file and build output beside them, loads it, then loads it again with a `source` setting in `lathe.config.json`.
then: Expects `scripts/seed.js` and `src/helpers.ts` as code-file-untraced gaps of the product, outside every domain, with the message naming the file; a `source` setting of `src/**/*.ts` leaving only `src/helpers.ts`; an empty `source` refused with "source must list globs of the source files"; and no such gap for a product with no source files.

title: A business outcome nothing that runs measures, and that names no measure outside the code, is a coverage gap
when: Removes the complete product's measured_by link; makes its one measuring test not automated yet; links a manual test instead; says how it is measured outside the code.
then: The gap is the product's with no problem, still there and saying why while the test is not automated, and gone with a manual test or a measure outside the code.

title: A test whose file lacks its ID is reported as an error
when: Loads the complete product with the invariant test's file not naming `EX-LEND-INV01-T`.
then: Expects the only gap to be `proved EX-LEND-INV01`, and no gaps when the file names the test.

title: A state outside the three, or none, is refused
when: Loads a test with the state someday, one with Manual, and one with no state.
then: Expects the first two refused as values outside automated, manual and not automated yet, and the third as a missing required column.

title: Only an automated test needs a file, and only a manual test gives a reason
when: Loads an automated test with no file, a manual test with no reason, a reason on an automated test, and a test not automated yet naming a file that does not exist.
then: Expects the first three refused, and the last to load with one test-file-missing warning and no error.

title: A level outside the five, or none, is refused
when: Loads a test with the level smoke, and one with no level.
then: Expects the first refused as a value outside the five levels, and the second as a missing required column.

title: A test is small unless it says volume or worst case, and marks itself smoke or external only by saying yes
when: Gives a test volume with both markers, worst case, small, and each marker as no.
then: Every test kind has the three optional columns; volume, worst case and the markers as yes load; small is refused as not one of the sizes, and a marker of no by its check.

title: A pattern rule is an obligation under a pattern, for proof alone
when: Loads the complete product with no pattern rule test.
then: Expects pattern_rule an obligation, its rule designed and built though nothing designs it, and only its proof missing.

title: A domain that does not follow the pattern does not owe its rules
when: Adds a second domain, `EX-SHOP`, whose use cases do not follow the complete product's pattern.
then: Expects a pattern rule total of 0 in `EX-SHOP`.

title: A domain's own pattern rule test proves the rule there alone
when: A second domain follows the pattern with no test of its own, then with one not automated yet.
then: Expects the rule proved in the first domain only, and not automated yet in the second once its test is.

title: Not-proved warnings name the pattern rule and the domain
when: Two domains owe a rule and neither proves it, then one has a test not automated yet.
then: Expects one not-proved warning per domain naming the rule and the domain, the second time saying the test there is not automated yet.

title: A pattern that no use case follows is a warning
when: Loads the complete product with its setting values, `follows` links and pattern rule tests removed, so no use case or domain follows its pattern.
then: Expects one `pattern-not-followed` warning on `EX-PAT-ACT`: "No use case or domain follows pattern EX-PAT-ACT, so its 1 rule is not counted in any domain's coverage."

title: An obligation outside every domain counts in Shared
when: Declares an obligation kind under the product, with one record.
then: Expects it counted and not proved in the product's Shared coverage, and no pattern rule there.

title: A test file names an ID only as a whole ID
when: Loads the complete product with `test/loans.test.ts` naming `EX-LEND-INV01-T2` but not `EX-LEND-INV01-T`.
then: Expects a `test-file-missing-id` problem on `EX-LEND-INV01-T` alone.

title: A test whose file lacks its ID, or is gone, is reported as an error
when: Loads tests whose files lack their IDs, are gone, or name them.
then: Expects a `test-file-missing-id` error, a `test-file-missing` error, and nothing for the test whose file names it.

title: A missing test file is an error, and a warning for a test not automated yet
when: Loads the complete product with the manual integration test naming the missing `manual/mail.md`, the domain service test not automated yet naming the missing `test/later.test.ts`, and the constraint test's file `test/email.test.ts` missing.
then: Expects test-file-missing as an error on `EX-INT01-T01` and `EX-VO01-C01-T` and a warning on `EX-LEND-DS01-T01`, the last saying "Constraint test EX-VO01-C01-T names the file test/email.test.ts, which does not exist."

title: A product kind's record that proves an obligation has its file checked as a test's
when: Loads a product with a script that designs a house rule and a rule check that proves it, first with neither file written, then with both files leaving their IDs out.
then: Expects test-file-missing and then test-file-missing-id to report the rule check alone, as errors, and never the script.

title: A test case naming no test whose file it is in is an error; one named in its describe or each rows is not
when: Loads a product whose test files hold test cases named by a test of the file, by a describe, by each rows, by a test of another file and by nothing, with Vitest and Playwright forms and a test written inside a string.
then: Expects a test-case-unnamed error for each unnamed test case and the one naming another file's test, with its file and line, and nothing for the rest.

title: A file a test names is read for test cases, whatever its name
when: Loads a product whose test records name a file outside the test globs that holds an unnamed test case.
then: Expects a test-case-unnamed error for it.

title: Each domain counts its own tests by state, which every test gives
when: Loads the complete product and reads the tests by state of its domain and of the product outside every domain.
then: Expects 11 automated, 2 manual and 0 not automated yet in `EX-LEND`, and 1 automated, the standard rule's test, outside every domain.

title: lathe check reports each domain's tests by state
when: Runs lathe check on the complete product with one test not automated yet.
then: Expects one tests line for the domain, after all of its obligation lines.

title: A domain that follows a pattern itself owes every one of its rules
when: A domain follows a pattern itself.
then: Expects every rule of the pattern counted and covered in `EX-LEND`.

title: A domain following a pattern itself and through a use case counts each rule once
when: A domain follows a pattern itself and through its use case.
then: Expects each rule counted once there.

title: A pattern may have no settings
when: A pattern with no settings is followed by a domain and by a use case that gives no setting values.
then: Expects no pattern-setting-missing, and its rule owed.

title: A use case that gives no value for one of its pattern's settings is an error naming the setting
when: Loads the complete product, then the same with every setting value removed, so its use case gives no value for its pattern's setting `record`.
then: Expects no `pattern-setting-missing` error first, then one naming the use case, the pattern and the setting.

title: A product's own kind may be an obligation
when: Declares one product kind an obligation and one not, with a record of each.
then: Expects the first counted, and not proved, and the second not counted.

title: The Tool Library still reads sensibly: its proof-only pattern rules are proved, with nothing asked for design
when: Loads `examples/tool-library`.
then: Expects no errors, every `TL-LEND` obligation designed, and its pattern rules counted for proof only with 3 of 3 proved.

title: A product kind named like one of Lathe's tables is refused
when: A product declares a kind named pattern_rule.
then: Expects the store to refuse it as a table name Lathe already has.

title: A use case that follows a pattern is not asked for requirements
when: Two use cases with no requirements, one following a pattern.
then: Expects use-case-without-requirement only for the one that follows nothing.

title: Each Pattern following command changes one following through its repository, and each interface runs the command it names
when: Builds the Pattern following aggregate's data set with its own commands, changes each kind, gives inputs of another shape, and runs commands as lathe pattern-following with flags, as their MCP tools and as POST /api/pattern-following/<command>.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the aggregate's own tables, each refused one to name its rule and reason and change no file, and each interface to run the command it names.

title: A pattern rule test naming a domain that does not follow the pattern is an error
when: Loads a pattern rule test naming a domain that does not follow the pattern, then has the domain follow it.
then: Expects a pattern-rule-test-outside-followers error naming the domain and pattern, and none once the domain follows it.

title: A manual test whose file names neither its ID, nor an ID it proves, nor its key is reported
when: Points the complete product's manual integration test at `manual/mail.md`, once with that file present but never naming the test, and once with no such file.
then: Expects a `manual-test-file-silent` warning on `EX-INT01-T01` when the file exists and never names it, and none when the file is missing.

title: The Reader sees how complete each domain is and what is undecided or broken
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a product's page in the app.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The Reader reads one obligation's chain
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a UC requirement's Trace stage.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The Reader reads every obligation under a record as a tree
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a domain's Trace stage and switch on Gaps only.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: Each obligation's chain holds what designs it, what builds it as built counts, its tests and their files, link by link
when: Loads the complete product.
then: Expects a UC requirement's steps, flow, view, operations and integration in design, its handlers and adapter in build, its test and the file naming it, with each link; a view requirement's building UI component and an invariant's rule in build; a policy's command and a constraint's value object in design; and a chain for every obligation and nothing else.

title: A flow step, command, query or UI component no obligation's chain reaches is a record-untraced gap
when: Loads the complete product, then one with a step that fulfills nothing, a command nothing invokes and a UI component that builds no view requirement.
then: Expects no record-untraced gap on the complete product, and on the other the step, the query only it invokes, the command and the UI component (as it builds no view requirement), never a handler or a test, each a gap and not a problem.

title: A product's traces read gives each obligation of its space the engine's chain, the gaps coverage reports and whether only proof is asked of it, and the records coverage reports untraced
when: Reads list-traces over two products with a run of the checks whose chains and coverage cover obligations of each product; then without a run; then through the CLI, the MCP tool and HTTP over a run of the checks.
then: Expects each product's obligations with their chains, gaps in order and proof-only flag, its untraced records and nothing of the other product, a refusal without a run, and the same answer from the CLI and HTTP.

title: The Reader reads coverage for every obligation kind and every test state
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a domain's page and a gap's record.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The Reader sees which pattern rules a domain owes and whether it proves each
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a domain's Patterns we follow and a pattern's page.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The Reader sees each domain's tests by state beside its coverage
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a product's page and a domain's page.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The Reader sees what designs, builds and proves a record
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Open a UC requirement's page, then one of its tests.
then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The record trace read gives an obligation's chain, its built marks and its standing where it is owed
when: Reads get-record-trace for an obligation over a checks' run.
then: Expects Designed by, Built by and Proved by from its chain, the build records that are built, and its gaps in its domain as coverage says.

title: The record trace read judges each of a use case's requirements in its domain
when: Reads get-record-trace for a use case.
then: Expects each UC requirement with its group and its judgment: what designs, builds and proves it, and its gaps.

title: The record trace read gives a test what it proves and its run by, and a test data set none
when: Reads get-record-trace for a test and for a test data set.
then: Expects the test's parent as what it proves and its level, state, file, size and markers; a test data set has no run by.

title: An endpoint handler's file that does not name its method and route is an error
when: Loads endpoints whose handlers' files name the route with its method, with another method, with the method too far away, as a regular expression, not at all, or are missing.
then: Expects an endpoint-route-not-in-file error for the other method, the far method and the unnamed route, naming the endpoint, route and file, and none for the rest.

title: A view whose route no component file names is an error
when: Loads views rendered by components whose files name the route another way, do not name it, or are missing, and a view with no route.
then: Expects a view-route-not-in-file error only for the view whose component file does not name its route.

title: A route the code serves with no endpoint or view is a gap
when: Loads a product whose handler file and router file serve routes by method calls, keys, comparisons and route constants, some with records and some without, and others only in comments.
then: Expects route-without-record gaps of the product for `/health`, `/tools/:id` and `DELETE /loans/:id`, each naming its file and line, and none for the commented route or `/catalog`; no router files by default and a `routers` that is not a list refused; and the recognizer reading `GET /a`, `/` and `/c/{}` but not a commented route or a plain string.

title: A table's file that lacks its name, a column or a key is a warning for each
when: Loads a product whose tables name a SQL file that defines one table whole, leaves out another's column and keys, and defines no third; and a view whose file selects its columns.
then: Expects table-schema-mismatch warnings for `member_id`, the primary key and the foreign key of `loans` and for no table `tools`; none once the file is written whole, apart from a foreign key to the wrong table; and with the file missing, technical-file-missing on all three tables and no table-schema-mismatch.

title: A table kept in a database whose file leaves out a column is a table-schema-mismatch warning
when: Loads the complete product with a schema file whose tables lack their columns.
then: Expects table-schema-mismatch warnings for each table it names, and only those.

title: A table's columns come from column names, field names, flattened value objects and children kept in the root's table
when: Gives an entity a field with a column name, one named in words, one typed by a value object of two fields, and a child kept in its root's table.
then: Expects exactly those columns, and the recognizer to read inline and table keys, indexes, ALTER TABLE, quoted names and the names a SELECT list gives with AS.

title: A table stored as a table with no file is a gap; one in browser storage is not
when: Clears a table's file, and keeps another in browser storage with no file.
then: Expects a table-without-file gap on the first only.

title: A package no record names is one gap on the product, until a record names it
when: Loads a product whose two package.json files list four packages across the four sections, one named on its adapter; then names the rest.
then: Expects one gap on the product naming the three others with their manifests, then no gap and no problem.

title: A record naming a package no manifest lists is an error
when: Loads an adapter naming a listed package and an unlisted one; then the same with no package.json at all.
then: Expects one package-not-in-manifest error naming the adapter and the unlisted package, then the adapter reported again.

title: A record naming a package no manifest lists is an error, as Lathe's checks report it
when: Loads the complete product with its adapter naming one package its package.json lists and one it does not.
then: Expects one package-not-in-manifest error, naming the adapter and the unlisted package.

title: Only a technical record names a package, a tooling record included
when: Loads a package on a use case, a name npm does not allow, and a package on a tooling record.
then: Expects package-use-technical and the table's CHECK to refuse the first two, and the tooling record to account for its package.

title: The manifests are the listed folders, or the root and the folders under it
when: Loads manifests at the root, one folder down, two folders down, under node_modules and in a hidden folder; then lists one folder; then a folder with none and one outside the root.
then: Expects the root and the folder directly under it found, only the listed one read, and each config mistake to stop the load naming the folder.
